These reports show a wide range of aging conditions (e.g., storage in N , in 2 ambient air, in air at 85˚C 85% R.H., MPP light-soaking) for various encapsulation materials (e.g., polymers, inorganic single and multilayer systems, in-grain encapsulation). Figure 25 illustrates that within the broad context of this sample population, despite our high initial PCE (21.65%) placing at the upper end of the scale (PCEs in the range of approx. 11% to 24%), our champion device stability is outperformed by other studies (Table 3). However, outstanding stability of over 10,000 hours (T90: Initial PCE >20%) is only attained in a controlled environment (i.e., dry air, dark) and significantly reduced (T97: 153 hours) when an identical device was aged under illumination and MPP tracking.92 As such, it is important to account for aging conditions when comparing stability metrics across studies.93 To this effect, data points were filtered to 14 devices reported across 10 publications that measure the operational lifetimes of 38/52 DE-EE0010241 Nicolas Gaillard PSCs by aging under conditions comparable to the ones used in our study (i.e., continuous illumination in ambient air and MPP tracking). Under these conditions, our result (PCE 21.65%: T90 of 1,430 hours) demonstrates the highest performance amongst thin-film encapsulated PSCs (Figure 26), on par with the historical trend of operational stabilities achieved with all encapsulation techniques.3 Figure 25: The PCE and stability of the champion PSC in this work (star) plotted alongside those of thin-film encapsulated PSC aged under varying aging conditions (Table 3). The device PCEs are presented in the figures using (a) initial values before aging and (b) final values after aging. Most devices maintained above 80% of their initial efficiencies after aging. Note that PCEs may not reflect the exact initial PCE of aged devices in certain instances due to limited details (e.g., only champion PCE reported). Some data points are not visible due to overlap. 39/52 DE-EE0010241 Nicolas Gaillard PSCs were also encapsulated with the semi-bonded Masterbond-based TCC and coated with a secondary-IZO electrode. The current density-voltage measurements before and after IZO/TCC coating for Masterbond-based TCC are presented in Table 14. Electrical measurements showed a slight reduction in PCE, mainly as a result of FF losses. The reduction is presumed to be a combination of high-temperature Masterbond lamination schedules (up to 80 ˚C) and the losses in conductivity due to insufficient microsphere exposure. Due to the time constraint, no further measurements were taken for Masterbond-based TCC-coated devices.
